item.title: 2026 Goombay — Sun Sep 13, 11:30 AM — YMI Cultural Center/Pack Square Park
item.description:
Goombay Festival returns to Asheville’s historic East End for a vibrant celebration of Black culture, music, food, art, and community! Rooted in the rich traditions of Asheville’s Black community, Goombay brings neighbors and visitors together for a weekend of unforgettable experiences—from live music and Go-Go to local vendors, art, dance, food, family activities, and the Ujima 5K. Presented by the YMI Cultural Center, Goombay is more than a festival—it is a celebration of heritage, resilience, creativity, and the people who continue to shape Western North Carolina. Come experience the energy, support Black-owned businesses and artists, reconnect with community, and celebrate the legacy of Asheville’s historic East End. Come for the culture. Stay for the community. Leave with the Goombay spirit. ymiculturalcenter.org/goombay
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

AmiciMusic presents "TRAGIC TRIOS" A Musical Commemoration of the 25th Anniversary of 9/11 — Sun Sep 13, 2:00 PM — St. Giles Chapel at Deerfield Retirement Community
item.description: Join us for this somber, but powerful tribute on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 tragedy. Violinist Frances Hsieh (from Charleston) and cellist Franklin Keel (from Asheville) will join me to perform two incredible Piano Trios that were composed at times of immense tragedy. Dmitri Shostakovich started his Second Piano Trio in 1943 after finding out about the death of his good friend, Ivan Solletinsky. As news spread about the Concentration Camps in Germany, Shostakovich expanded the work to include Jewish themes and the Trio turned into an incredibly powerful tribute to the Holocaust victims and a despairing look at humanity. Bedrich Smetana’s Piano Trio in G Minor was composed shortly after two of his young girls had passed away. Smetana pours his grief into this amazing Trio that highlights human suffering, but also the will to keep living even in the face of unimaginable horror. item.description:
Fall Garden Photography Workshop with Cami Calnan Wednesday, October 7 | 10am – 12pm Register Here!
Do you want to learn to take better seasonal fall photos in the gardens? Join us for a hands-on workshop where we use whatever camera you are working with to learn tips, tricks, and techniques to take the photos you are hoping to capture. Bring your phone, a point and shoot camera, digital SLR or film SLR camera. This class is for all levels of photographers. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Camilla Calnan is an Asheville based photographer since 2000 and has been a longtime friend and supporter of the NC Arboretum.
